operators.notes: Shipdate range already applied by shared scan. Only discount range and quantity filter remain. Evaluate all three predicates in a single fused pass with short-circuit evaluation; discount predicates first (cheaper branch, higher combined selectivity ~28%) then quantity.
No GROUP BY — each thread maintains a single double accumulator. Final merge sums across threads (trivial). Use Kahan summation for numerical stability on ~1.2M multiply-accumulate operations.

parallelism.notes: Shared scan delivers morsels of ~64K rows. Each thread applies residual filters and accumulates into a thread-local double. Final merge is a single reduction across thread accumulators — negligible cost. No synchronization needed during the hot loop.

data_structures.notes: One double per thread, cache-line padded to avoid false sharing. Total memory: 64 threads * 64 bytes = 4KB.

notes: Extremely lightweight tail. The shared scan does the heavy lifting (HDD I/O + shipdate filtering). This tail is pure CPU: three cheap column comparisons + one multiply-accumulate per surviving row. Entire tail fits in L1 cache. Expected wall-clock contribution < 20ms on 64 cores.
